title: Caribbean Rice and Peas
subtitle: Jamaican coconut rice with kidney beans
excerpt: Caribbean rice and peas is a staple of Jamaican Sunday cooking. Rice is cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans -- confusingly called peas in Jamaica -- and seasoned with thyme, garlic, and allspice. It is the essential side dish for jerk chicken and most Caribbean mains.
sourceNotes: Rice and peas is cooked every Sunday in Jamaica, hence its reputation as Sunday rice. The use of kidney beans -- called peas -- rather than actual garden peas is the defining feature. Coconut milk and whole Scotch bonnet chilli cooked in the pot are the key flavour elements.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale up easily. The ratios stay the same.

content.text: Add the whole scotch bonnet uncut if you want the fragrance and mild warmth without full heat. If you want it spicy, prick it once with a knife before adding. Remove it before serving.

items.prepNote: use kidney beans (tinned) -- called peas in the Caribbean
use a 400ml tin of coconut milk
use 1 whole scotch bonnet chilli, uncut

content.text: Pour the coconut milk into a large saucepan. Add 300ml of water. Bring to a simmer.
Add the spring onions, garlic, thyme, allspice, scotch bonnet, and salt. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the drained kidney beans. Stir in the rinsed rice.
Bring back to the boil, stirring once. Reduce to the lowest heat. Cover tightly and cook for 18 minutes.
Remove from heat. Rest for 5 minutes without lifting the lid. Remove and discard the spring onions, thyme sprigs, and scotch bonnet. Fluff the rice with a fork and serve.

items.cause: Coconut milk alone is too thick; not enough liquid
items.fix: Always add water alongside the coconut milk in the ratio given

items.symptom: Rice at the bottom is wet while the top is cooked
items.fix: The lowest possible heat is needed; use a heat diffuser if your hob runs hot

items.symptom: Scotch bonnet made the rice very spicy
items.cause: It was cut or pierced before adding
items.fix: Keep the scotch bonnet whole and uncut for fragrance without extreme heat

content.text: Rice and peas is cooked every Sunday in homes across Jamaica. It is the essential side dish of Jamaican food culture. Without rice and peas, it is not a proper Sunday dinner. Variations exist across the Caribbean -- Barbados uses pigeon peas, Trinidad uses black-eyed peas, and Cuba uses black beans.
